English as an Additional Language (EAL)
At ACS Egham, we believe that achieving proficiency in academic English is more than just overcoming a challenge—it’s about celebrating the advantages of being multilingual.
We believe that students’ unique language profiles are a fact, a right, and a valuable resource for individuals, the school community, and the world. Our English as an Additional Language (EAL) programme helps students develop the fluency in English they need to thrive in a global community and succeed in International Baccalaureate Primary Years (IBPYP), Middle Years (IBMYP), Diploma (IBDP), and Career-related Programmes (IBCP).
The EAL Programme
The EAL programme is personalised to each English language learner.
Intensive English Courses
Focused, small-group lessons designed to rapidly build foundational English skills, vocabulary, and grammatical accuracy. Students have timetabled lessons led by an EAL specialist teacher, progressing rapidly from emergent to capable and then proficient levels of listening, reading, speaking, and writing.
Critical Academic Language Proficiency
Specialist teachers provide in-class support for IB courses across all academic subject areas. Students learn how to analyse complex texts, participate in academic discussions, write sophisticated essays, and understand nuanced instructions crucial for success in advanced courses.
Monitoring Student Progress
Each EAL learner is supported by a case manager who closely monitors their development of Basic Interpersonal Communication Skills and academic language proficiency. Students become multi-literate, increasing their competence in listening, reading, speaking, and writing. EAL support empowers them to:
In-class Support (UDL)
Our EAL specialists collaborate with classroom teachers, using the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework to ensure that EAL students can access information and demonstrate their learning in receptive, productive, and interactive tasks. Students continue to improve grammar and accuracy, vocabulary and pronunciation, and organisation. They develop sophisticated understanding of meaning, purpose, audience, register, and structure of English texts.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
For our IB Diploma Students, there are opportunities to maintain and develop their home language(s) through School Support Self-Taught Literature courses, one of the pathways that can lead toward the IB Bilingual Diploma.
Language fluency grows through interactions with peers. Our extensive programme of co-curricular activities (including competitive sports teams, performing arts productions, and volunteering with the community) provides opportunities for students to practise English in engaging, real-world settings.
Many languages are supported by after school Home Language Enrichment opportunities.
Achieving Excellence in IBDP and Beyond
The EAL programme helps students succeed in IBDP courses by improving their academic English skills and supporting their literacy in their home language(s). As a result, our multilingual students achieve high academic success. Every year, graduates go on to attend top universities in the UK, the US, and around the world.
Who is the EAL Programme for?
The EAL programme is designed for motivated students joining ACS Egham who have a broad range of English language proficiency. It is available to qualified students who are ready to engage in academic and co-curricular activities, contribute to our multilingual community, and succeed in rigorous academic courses, including an opportunity to earn the prestigious IB Bilingual Diploma.
Find out more about EAL at ACS Egham

ACS Egham is celebrating an outstanding achievement in entrepreneurship after its student team won 1st Place at the Business@School International Finals in Milan with their startup idea “RhythmBase”.
After progressing through multiple stages of the prestigious competition, founded by the Boston Consulting Group in 1998, the team of five students secured their place in the international final in Milan, where they presented their business concept to a panel of senior judges from global organisations, and prevailed against teams from Italy, Albania, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

RhythmBase
RhythmBase was created to solve a real challenge facing independent musicians. The platform combines artist management, gig booking, venue connections, analytics, income tracking, and AI-powered tools into a single ecosystem.
The students’ approach to entrepreneurship focused on identifying a genuine market need and developing a practical solution. Through extensive market research, customer interviews, and business planning, they validated their concept and built a compelling case for growth.
Presenting on an international stage in Milan, the team demonstrated the confidence, creativity, and innovation that successful entrepreneurship requires.
Developing Entrepreneurship Skills Through Real-World Learning
Over the course of a year, the team developed skills in market analysis, financial forecasting, product development, public speaking, and strategic planning. Their success reflects ACS Egham’s commitment to experiential learning and preparing students for an increasingly complex global economy.
As the UK’s first IB Continuum School, ACS Egham introduces students to these entrepreneurship skills from a young age, and continuously reinforces them throughout their time at school. Students can choose to study the Career-related IBCP pathway from age 16, an internationally respected qualification which directly tests and strengths these skills for futures in entrepreneurship and commercial success.
ACS Egham Curriculum
About Business@School
Founded in 1998 by Boston Consulting Group (BCG), Business@School introduces senior high school students to the world of business and entrepreneurship. Through three competition phases, students gain hands-on experience developing business ideas, analysing markets, and presenting solutions to industry experts.
Supported by coaches from leading companies, the programme helps students develop the entrepreneurial skills, confidence, and practical experience needed for future success.
Celebrating an Entrepreneurship Achievement
Winning the Business at School International Finals is an extraordinary accomplishment and a proud moment for the entire ACS Egham community.
The RhythmBase team has shown what student entrepreneurship can achieve through dedication, collaboration, and innovation. Their success in Milan serves as an inspiration for future student entrepreneurs and highlights the transformative power of experiential learning.
Congratulations to the RhythmBase team on becoming international champions and ambassadors for entrepreneurship at ACS Egham.

Academic Excellence
Explore our Inspection Reports – your window into our commitment to excellence in education. We proudly present the outcomes of our rigorous inspections by independent regulatory bodies.
At ACS Egham, we believe in innovation, and the relentless pursuit of educational excellence; our inspection reports highlight our strengths, affirm our standards, and showcase areas of continual improvement.
A top-notch IB programme, 36 acres of glorious parkland on the outskirts of London and a welcoming, internationally minded ‘glocal’ community.
Good Schools Guide Review 2025
ISI Report 2024
Overview

Key findings: Staff, Programmes, and Facilities
Overview
We are delighted to share the findings of our 2024 ISI Inspection, and congratulate our students, staff, and parents for making us an ‘Excellent’ place to learn, work, and collaborate.
Inspections provide valuable feedback on our continual improvement goals. They represent a key aspect of our Education Quality Framework, assures ACS Egham and the wider community that the school meets a wide range of rigorous national and international standards.
ACS Egham meets all ISI standards for:
leadership, management and governance;
quality of education, training and recreation;
safeguarding and child protection.
Key findings: ACS Egham students
Key findings: Staff, Programmes, and Facilities
Leaders create an open culture in school so that difference is understood and respected. The pupil-led group, ‘Jags for Justice’, promotes inclusion and understanding of difference through creating online and printed resources. Pupils feel confident to be themselves because they value the non-judgemental approach of staff and other pupils.
ACS Egham CLP Report 2024
The personal development of students is excellent. The cultural diversity within the school and the emphasis on community service develops strong social and cultural awareness.

Partnerships
ACS Partnerships
As a group of schools with an inspiring, engaged community and an international ethos, ACS is uniquely placed to build meaningful educational partnerships that advance education for school age children, supporting local and global communities wherever it can.
At ACS Egham, we have different partnerships that provide opportunities for students to access enhanced education not otherwise available to them and for teachers to develop teaching excellence.
Our school was thrilled recently to win a silver award from the Global Good awards in recognition of its partnerships locally and internationally.
Our Partnerships Impact
Of student interaction
of teacher training
of outreach box usage
COMMUNITY COLLABORATION
We collaborate with partner schools locally and globally. Partner schools use our facilities for many different occasions and uses from hosting a sports day, attending our Forest Schools, to multi-school learning and activity days hosted at our campuses.
These include the SATRO FEST, which welcomed 21 Surrey Senior schools for a day of STEM challenge, Destination Imagination UK, local primary school groups STEM festival and countless school swimming galas.
ACS is committed to continuing to share resources, facilities, expertise, and ideas with partner schools and delighted to collaborate to enrich both local and ACS students’ learning experiences.
PARTNERSHIP EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES
ACS creates memorable experiences for students to come together and learn through major events.
STEAM 2024 was a celebration of all things STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics). 10,000 students attended a day at Thorpe Park theme park, learning from many exciting corporate exhibitors such as the Royal Air Force, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra (RPO) before enjoying the rides.
Other activities include: young carer days at our campuses; Elite football residential camps in partnerships with London premier league clubs; ‘A Night at the West End’ with 12 partner schools and 250 local school children performing alongside partners Performing Perfectly and the RPO.
Teaching Excellence
ACS shares teaching excellence and a deep understanding of best practice to empower teachers within partner schools, often with limited or stretched resources, to advance their own skillset and students’ educational experience.
ACS provides expertise and training in a number of ways:
Partnerships in action

Project Nepal
What is Project Nepal?
Project Nepal is ACS Egham’s humanitarian initiative, launched in 2014, with a mission to foster students’ commitment to service, social justice, and community engagement.
Our goal is to empower students to work meaningfully with diverse communities while involving the entire school in creating lasting impact.
To date, we have provided essential funding for educational initiatives in Nepal and offered ACS Egham students opportunities for social action—enabling them to contribute to sustainable change.
Get involved: Donate to Project Nepal
Project Gallery
Project Timeline
Year 1 (2015)
38 students aged 15-17 travelled to Nepal to work on Shree Mahendra Primary School, here they:
installed, sanded and painted a privacy gate;
painted 7 classrooms with educational murals;
taught lessons in English;
donated Physical Education equipment.
Year 2-4 (2016-2018)
31 students travelled to Panchkal, Nepal to support a rural primary school serving 75 students up to age 10, our team:
secured earthquake-related foundation issues;
designed and installed a community football pitch;
installed playground equipment;
developed an after-school club;
taught lessons in English;
supplied stationary and PE equipment;
painted 5 classrooms.
Year 5 (2018)
20 students travelled to Mkushi, Zambia to support the Itala Foundation School. Whilst out there, our team:
assisted with food purchasing and preparation.
Year 6-7 (2019-2021)
Due to the global pandemic, ACS students were unable to travel to Nepal.
The construction on the building project was put on pause during the various lockdowns.
Work resumed as soon as was possible and we continued to support our scholars.
Year 8 (2022)
Return to Nepal in the Spring break of 2022 with 36 high school students from grades 9, 10 and 11. ACS Egham students:
Year 9 (2023)
Project Nepal had a very successful and memorable trip during Spring break 2023 to Nepal. Our adventure started with a 3-day trek in Chisapani National Park and Kutumsang area. We were treated daily to amazing views of the Himalayan Mountain range and surrounding areas.
Over the course of the trip, ACS Students:
Year 10 (2024)
During the October break of 2024, Project Nepal embarked on another unforgettable journey. Twenty-six ACS students, joined by four students from our partner organization, Football Family, spent two inspiring weeks in Nepal. The team worked on a meaningful construction project at the Ajad School in Bhaktapur. Thanks to the funds we raised, we were able to pave the school’s multipurpose area, install a boundary fence for the junior section, and brighten the exterior walls with colourful, joyful murals.
Beyond the construction work, our students formed heartfelt connections with the students at Ajad, building friendships that transcended borders. After completing the project, we took time to explore Nepal’s natural beauty. Our group trekked through Chisapani National Park and the Kutumsang area, where we were rewarded with breathtaking views of the Langtang region, nestled in the foothills of the Himalayas.
We also had the chance to reconnect with our legacy scholarship students at Sarabamangal College in Panchkal and in Kathmandu. Witnessing firsthand the positive impact of Project Nepal’s financial support on their lives was both moving and motivating.
We returned home with unforgettable memories and the deep satisfaction of knowing that our efforts are truly making a difference.

English as an Additional Language (EAL)
At ACS Egham, the Lower School’s English as an Additional Language (EAL) programme supports young learners in a welcoming environment in which they can make friends and engage with the school’s curriculum—preparing them for success.
Specialist EAL Teaching
We recognise the unique strengths that EAL learners bring, including their cultural and personal experiences, and we use these assets to create a positive and supportive learning environment.
Our dedicated EAL specialists work closely with Lower School students across a range of English language competencies, providing personalised support to help build confidence and meet essential content learning goals. Each student’s progress is carefully monitored to ensure they receive the appropriate guidance.
English Language Learners and the IBPYP
Early and primary years students learn English in a supportive immersion setting, in which they use their full linguistic repertoire (all languages they know) to learn and communicate.
We recognise that multilingual students think and express themselves fluidly, drawing on their different languages as one interconnected system. In the IBPYP, this natural process—known as ‘trans-languaging’—helps create a more inclusive and engaging learning environment, where students feel empowered to speak, belong, and thrive as they learn English together.
To support this, our planning reflects the diverse needs of all learners. We offer multiple means of engagement, representation, and expression, ensuring that every student can access the curriculum and demonstrate their understanding in ways that suit them best.
The EAL Programme in Lower School
Small group lessons that teach content and language together
Trained teachers who understand the needs of multilingual students
Home Language Enrichment for many global languages (optional after school activity)
In-class support from specialist teachers
EAL Assessment and Academic Progression
In Lower School, we assess students across four key domains: speaking, listening, reading, and writing. These areas give us a well-rounded view of each student’s language development.
For students new to English, we support their progression from Basic Interpersonal Communication Skills (BICS)—used in everyday conversation—to Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (CALP), which is needed for success in the classroom.
Students with some English proficiency are guided toward greater academic fluency, while also encouraged to continue developing their home language. We value multilingualism and use assessment to inform targeted support, ensuring every learner can thrive both linguistically and academically.

Ready to Participate
There’s something for everyone at ACS Egham; our vibrant array of clubs and activities ranges from arts to sports and craft clubs.
Our co-curricular activities (CCA) programme focuses on five key areas, including sports, the arts, STEAM, International Mindedness and Debate and Personal Challenge and Leadership. Students are given the opportunity to explore their passions, forge lasting connections beyond the classroom and engage with our diverse community.
The list below provides an example of the activities on offer within these key areas, and are constantly updated to accommodate demand.
Upper School Clubs and Activities
Sports
Team Jaguar provides our students with a programme of high quality, values-driven sporting, promoting an active healthy lifestyle and engaging students in team-building and collaboration. A few of our sports clubs include:
Fall season: Football Volleyball Cross Country
Winter season: Basketball Cross Country
The Arts
The Arts thrive at ACS Egham. We offer a number of activities, including Voice in a Million at the O2 Arena, our annual school production (with recent shows including Sweeney Todd, and A Midsummer Night’s Dream) as well as a number of musical and creative groups.
Co-curricular performing arts
School Productions (musical and non-musical)

Individual music lessons
STEAM
STEAM stands for “Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Mathematics”. We take a whole school interdisciplinary approach, that reflects the importance of design and technology in today’s world. Our co-curricular activities enable students to explore and develop their individual interests within this subject area, to think imaginatively and independently.
Coding Club
Digital leaders
Rocket Club
and more…
International Mindedness and Debate
In our Model United Nations Club (MUN), we debate topics of international concern. As part of this, students can attend conferences each year in The Hague and other cities, where they debate the world’s most pressing issues with thousands of other students. its all part of our commitment to educating the whole student so that they’re ready for tomorrow.
Personal Challenge and Leadership
At ACS Egham, the Duke of Edinburgh (DofE) programme provides students with an enriching experience that prepares them for future success. Many students have achieved Bronze, Silver, and Gold awards, gaining recognition for their community service and adventurous expeditions.
Those who sign up engage in a variety of activities, including volunteering in community projects and environmental conservation, participation in team sports and fitness challenges, and developing skills in music, arts, cooking, and coding. The programme also features hiking and camping expeditions in South Downs and Surrey Hills.
Open to students in Grades 9-12, registration occurs each September, with expeditions typically taking place from March to June. Information sessions and guidance from DofE coordinators, along with training days by Adventure Life Signs, ensure students are well-prepared for the challenges they may face.
Our staff are highly experience and offer invaluable support to those taking part, supporting them in attaining valuable life skills, such as: leadership; teamwork; time management; problem-solving; critical thinking; enhanced physical fitness and a strong sense of community engagement and social responsibility.

Curriculum
An IB Education in the heart of Surrey
ACS Egham students and staff have a genuine drive for excellence. As an IB school, we prize holistic education, internationalism and communication.
ACS Egham Upper School students follow the International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (IBMYP) before choosing between the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) or the International Baccalaureate Career-related Programme (IBCP).
It is an education framework designed to develop both learning and life skills, providing a seamless, globally recognised route to success – both in and out of the classroom.
Our IB Programmes
IB Middle Years Programme (IBMYP)
The IBMYP develops critical thinking and challenges students to reflect on their learning experience. The programme encourages students to make practical connections between their studies and the real world within a framework of eight subject groups.
IB Diploma Programme (IBDP)
The IBDP fosters critical thinking and independent learning in students. The IBDP assesses more than just examination techniques, it encourages a breadth and depth of learning that students can carry forward.
IB Career-related Programme (IBCP)
The IBCP encourages students to specialise in an area of choice. Students are prepared for career-specific pathways, and their academic research and communication skills are developed through the Reflective Project.
ACS High School Diploma
All ACS Egham students who successfully complete the relevant studies receive an accredited High School Diploma, which underpins the curriculum in Grades 9-12. As part of this, students choose from an extensive range of traditional and contemporary subjects, to create stimulating programmes of study that reflect their interests. The ACS High School Diploma meets the admission requirements of US colleges and universities.
Assessment
In Upper School, we monitor progress through a range of school-based and externally benchmarked assessments. We offer meaningful assessment that nurtures students’ love for learning. At ACS Egham, assessment is inherently more flexible and designed to be more individualistic than other curriculum frameworks. It consists of a variety of ongoing assessment techniques.

IB Career-related Programme
Studying the IBCP
Specifically developed for students who want to engage in career-related learning during their time at ACS Egham, while gaining transferable skills in applied knowledge, critical thinking, communication, and cross-cultural engagement.
Today’s careers make great demands on graduates. The IBCP prepares students to meet those demands head-on in the form of self-confidence, accomplished personal and professional skills, and understanding of global languages and the ability to make ethical decisions.
The IBCP leads to higher education, apprenticeships, or employment. The IBCP components and certificate are increasingly valued as university entrance credentials.
IBCP Subject Areas
IBCP students at ACS Egham undertake a minimum of two IB Diploma (IBDP) courses, core studies, and a career-related study.
Career-related study (Business, Enterprise, and Entrepreneurship) supports the programme’s academic strength and provides practical, real-world approaches to learning. Core studies help students develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes required for lifelong learning.
IBCP students must complete 3 core elements
Two or three IBDP courses
Students in the IBCP framework choose IB Diploma Programme courses from various subject groups, studying them at standard or higher levels. Typically, students take three courses relevant to their career-related studies. All IBCP students must take at least two IBDP courses, including Sciences at Standard or Higher level.
Career-related study
Complete a Level 3 IB-approved course, independently assessed and meeting IB criteria for accreditation. ACS Egham has chosen the BTEC Level 3 National Diploma in Business, Enterprise and Entrepreneurship by Pearson (equivalent to 2 Higher Level IB subjects). This qualification is assessed through internal tasks and formal exams. Please refer to the course specification for additional details.
IBCP Core
The IBCP Personal Professional Skills course equips students with transferable life skills for navigating the 21st-century world. Community Engagement involves planning, executing, and reflecting on community service, fostering skill development. Language and Cultural Studies at ACS Egham includes learning British Sign Language (BSL) for diversity and inclusivity and aims to create a deeper cultural understanding of an acquired language. A Reflective Project prompts students to address ethical dilemmas from their career-related study, submitted in various formats.
Why choose the IBCP for your child?
IBCP students at ACS Egham are prepared for an ever-changing world of work, asking them to consider new perspectives, engage in learning that makes a positive difference.
The IBCP is a high quality programme of international education that will help your child to:
About the IBCP
What is the IBCP?
The IBCP is a flexible educational framework that combines academic study with career-related learning. In an ever-changing job market, skills valued by employers—such as creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, and problem-solving—are at the core of the IBCP curriculum. Students receive professional guidance and support, including participating in workshops led by industry professionals.
What are the main components of the IBCP?
The IBCP consists of three core components:
Career-related study: Students follow a vocational course or qualification that aligns with their career interests.
IB Diploma Programme courses: Students take a minimum of two IB Diploma subjects.
Personal and Professional Skills (PPS): This core component helps develop skills needed for the workplace, such as communication, teamwork, collaboration, ethics, and problem-solving.
How does the IBCP differ from the IB Diploma Programme (IBDP)?
In the IBDP, students are required to study six varied courses, one from each of the IBDP subject groups, to enable them to gain a more well-rounded qualification ahead of starting university and entering the workplace. This offers them the opportunity to explore what they are passionate about before they select a specific subject for university.
In the IBCP, students can select up to 3 subjects of the six IBDP subject groups, which might include studying multiple arts subjects, for example. As it is always recommended that for university requirements, students undertake some maths and some English, ACS Egham students study DP English language and Literature and develop their vocational maths in the Personal and Business finance unit.
What are the assessment methods used in the IBCP?
Assessment in the IBCP includes both internal and external evaluations. Students are assessed on their performance in their vocational studies, IBDP subjects, and the core components, with a focus on both academic knowledge and practical skills.
Can I continue to university after completing the IBCP?
The IB is widely accepted by top universities around the world. What sets students apart in the IBCP is that their career related study gives them a professional portfolio and a range of experiences in industry that will stand out in their college applications and personal statements. The industry-orientated, creative approach to building a portfolio with a range of skills is recognised by universities as a strong indicator of a student who is prepared to extend their own learning, in a similar way to their own university level courses.
What skills will I develop through the IBCP?
Students in the IBCP will develop a range of skills, including critical thinking, communication, collaboration, ethics, and problem-solving, which are essential for success in both the workplace and further studies.
What does ACS Egham offer for the IBCP?
IBCP students at ACS Egham undertake a minimum of two IB Diploma (IBDP) courses, core studies, and a career-related study. The Career-related study offered is BTEC Level 3 National Diploma in Business, Enterprise, and Entrepreneurship (this has the UCAS equivalence of 2 IBDP Higher Level subjects.)
I have been accepted into a work experience placement at J.P. Morgan in London... without the IBCP I don't believe I would have received an offer. It has had a great impact on my knowledge and understanding of enterprise and entrepreneurship, and I look forward to the following years in the IBCP.

IB Diploma Programme
Studying the IBDP
Our approach to learning in the upper years addresses students’ intellectual, social, emotional and physical wellbeing.
The International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) is an academically-challenging programme that ensures students aged 16-18 are ready for success at university and beyond. It has gained recognition and respect from the world’s leading universities due to the fact that IBDP students take responsibility for their own learning, developing critical and creative thinking as well as collaboration, research, self-management and communication skills.
As a group of schools, we have been teaching the IBDP for over fifty years, and many of our teachers are examiners for the programme. Therefore, we have the expertise and knowledge to support and guide students, enabling them to excel and achieve excellent results.
IBDP Subject Areas
The IBDP’s broad and balanced curriculum requires students to study six subjects during their final two years of school – three at higher level and three at standard level.
The curriculum includes:
IBDP results are based on a combination of end-of-course examinations and internally and externally-marked coursework.
Studies in Language and Literature
Language Acquisition
Mathematics
Sciences
The Arts
Individuals and Societies
IBDP Students must complete 3 core elements
Theory of Knowledge
A 100 hour course taught over two years about critical thinking and inquiry into the nature of knowledge. It is assessed through an oral presentation and a 1600-word essay
The Extended Essay
A 4000-word independent research essay into a topic that the student has a particular interest or passion in.
Creativity, Activity and Service (CAS)
Students take part in a range of experiences and at least one project. For many this will involve music, drama, sport, service in the local community and collaboration with our partner schools.
About the IBDP
Why choose the IBDP for your child?
The IBDP is an internationally-recognised qualification that provides additional evidence to support university applications.
The IB is highly regarded by leading universities around the globe thanks to its transferability, rigour and breath of study. Research studies have shown that IB Diploma students are more likely to gain entry to top-level universities than entrants with A-levels or other qualifications.
The IBDP is a high quality programme of international education that will help your child to:
At ACS Egham, we have an expert team of University & College Counsellors who assist students in finding the right “fit” for their future university studies.
What is the difference between the IBDP and A-levels?
The IBDP is not a programme that relies on standardised textbooks and rote learning. It is an enquiry-based programme that requires students to think independently, be creative and apply problem-solving skills to real-world situations.
Students are required to study six courses to enable them to gain a more well-rounded qualification ahead of starting university and entering the workplace. This offers them the opportunity to explore what they are passionate about before they select a specific subject for university.
In addition to the chosen subjects, IB students must complete the Theory of Knowledge, Creative, Action and Service (CAS), and the Extended Essay components. These encourage self-directed learning, providing students with the skills they need to thrive at university and in their future careers.
How is the IBDP assessed?
The IBDP is assessed using a combination of internal and external assessments to ensure a comprehensive evaluation of a student’s capabilities and prepare them for university education and beyond.
Each subject is graded on a scale of 1 to 7, with 7 being the highest. Students can earn up to 45 points, with 42 points from six subjects (each graded up to 7 points) and 3 additional points from the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay. To earn the diploma, students must achieve a minimum of 24 points.
The Core Components are also assessed:
Is the IBDP accepted by UK and US universities?
The IBDP helps students gain offers from prestigious universities around the world, including all UK universities. High education institutions in more than 90 countries accept students based on their IBDP credentials, while many US public and private colleges and universities offer credit or accelerated courses of study in the light of strong IBDP results.
How can the IBDP help my child’s university application?
Research has shown that students graduating with the IB Diploma have a 57% greater likelihood of attending one of the top 20 UK universities, compared to students who study the traditional A-Levels. Studies show that IB students are 21% more likely to be admitted into the United States’ most prestigious universities.
A report, by the Higher Education Statistics Agency in the UK, shows that an IB student is more likely to gain a first-class honours degree than an A-Level student (23% versus 19% respectively).
A recent survey asked 80 UK university admissions officers (representing almost half of universities in the UK) which entry qualification their university preferred. The majority of these universities believed the IB Diploma was the better preparation for university and the workplace. Both in the UK and globally, the IB Diploma is consistently rated as the best qualification for university as it provides students with the skills they need to thrive in higher education.

IB Diploma Courses and High School Diploma
Students may choose an alternative pathway to the IB Diploma Programme, while still undertaking the academically rigorous IB Curriculum. For a variety of reasons, the Diploma Programme pattern of study may not be the best or most appropriate pathway for all students and IB Courses may be a viable alternative. This may be a good option for students who wish to rely on the strength of their High School Diploma transcript and as such do not need to meet the pass conditions of the IB Diploma Programme.
Initially, students are required to choose six subjects in order to meet the ACS High School Diploma minimum credits, however, at a later point in the programme students can choose to take fewer subjects. Students are required to take Theory of Knowledge in Grade 11 and are required to undertake CAS in both Grades 11 and 12.
I could speak at length about why I would recommend the International Baccalaureate (IB) over other curriculums in the UK, but to keep it concise: the IB was challenging and sometimes overwhelming, yet I believe it adequately prepared me for further education and the working environment. The IB taught me time management and organisational skills, making university life more manageable regarding completing assessments on time and preparing for seminars. Furthermore, the focus on critical thinking and analysis in the IB was particularly beneficial for me as a law student, as I had already developed foundational skills that support my work in drafting cases and witness statements for mock court trials.
